prompt: What is Microsoft Entra ID, in relation to an Azure tenant?
hint: Which existed first?

choices.text: A paid add-on a subscription switches on
choices.why: Nothing is switched on: the directory comes with the tenant, before any subscription.

choices.text: A resource created in a resource group of each subscription
choices.why: The directory is above every subscription, not inside one.

choices.text: A replacement for Azure Active Directory with different endpoints
choices.why: It is the same product renamed in 2023; endpoints and error codes stayed.

choices.text: The directory every tenant already is, from its creation
choices.why: Right. The same directory serves Microsoft 365 and every work sign-in.

prompt: Why could the lab fetch the discovery document of `organizations` with no sign-in at all?
hint: What does a program need before it can send somebody to sign in?

choices.text: It is public on purpose: it says where to sign in
choices.why: Right. Every OpenID Connect provider publishes it at the same path.

choices.text: Because `organizations` is a test tenant Microsoft leaves open
choices.why: It is not a tenant: it stands for any work or school tenant.

choices.text: Because the lab's CLI holds a cached token
choices.why: The lab has never signed in, and `curl` sends no token anyway.

choices.text: Because Microsoft Graph forwards anonymous reads
choices.why: Graph was not asked; the answer came from `login.microsoftonline.com`.

prompt: Match each field of the discovery document to what it is for.
hint: One is for a person in a browser, one for a program.

pairs.right: where a person is sent to sign in
where a program asks for a token
the public keys that sign tokens
who a token will say issued it

right_distractors: the list of users in the tenant

prompt: Every Entra ID error code starts with the prefix ___, left over from the old name.
hint: It came before 90002.

prompt: What did `AADSTS90002` say about `aaaabbbb-0000-cccc-1111-dddd2222eeee`?
hint: Read the error's first sentence.

choices.text: That the tenant exists but refuses anonymous requests
choices.why: The discovery document is public; a tenant that existed would have answered.

choices.text: That the id is not a valid GUID
choices.why: It is a well-formed GUID. The refusal was *not found*.

choices.text: That no tenant has that id
choices.why: Right. Which is why the course can use it for the shop.

choices.text: That the lab must run `az login` first
choices.why: That message comes from the CLI. This one came from Entra ID itself.

prompt: An audit script records who changed each resource by user principal name. Bia marries and her name becomes `bia.lima@shop.example`. What breaks?
hint: Which of her two names never changes?

choices.text: Nothing: Entra ID rewrites the old name in every log
choices.why: Nothing rewrites a log, and the script's own records are its own.

choices.text: Her past changes no longer join to her
choices.why: Right. The object id is the stable one; the name was the wrong key.

choices.text: She loses her group memberships
choices.why: Memberships point at the object id, which did not change.

choices.text: She can no longer sign in until an administrator approves
choices.why: She signs in with the new name at once.

prompt: The shop's accountant works for an outside firm and is invited into the tenant. What type of user is she?
hint: She signs in with her own organisation's account.

choices.text: A service principal
choices.why: That is a program's identity, lesson 7. She is a person.

choices.text: A member with a shorter licence
choices.why: Members belong to the tenant; she belongs to another organisation.

choices.text: A guest, signing in with her firm's account
choices.why: Right. Her name carries `#EXT#`, and the shop never holds her password.

choices.text: A managed identity
choices.why: Managed identities belong to Azure resources, lesson 8.

prompt: Why give a role to a group rather than to the person?
hint: The rule is about leaving.

choices.text: Roles cannot be given to individual users
choices.why: They can. The rule is a choice, not a limit.

choices.text: Leaving the group removes the access with nobody remembering to
choices.why: Right. A permission given to a person stays until somebody remembers it.

choices.text: Groups cost less in the licence
choices.why: The argument is about removal, not price.

choices.text: A group signs in once for all its members
choices.why: A group never signs in; its members do, each as themselves.

prompt: Which kind of group does the shop use to grant access to Azure resources?
hint: One kind exists for collaboration.

choices.text: Security groups, which exist for access
choices.why: Right. They are for access, and can hold users, devices and service principals.

choices.text: Microsoft 365 groups, since every user has one
choices.why: Their members joined to share a calendar, which is the wrong reason to hold access.

choices.text: Administrative units
choices.why: Those scope directory roles; they do not receive Azure roles.

choices.text: Distribution lists
choices.why: Those deliver mail and appear nowhere in the lesson's table.

prompt: A dynamic group uses `user.department -eq "Engineering"`. Who could now put somebody into it?
hint: The rule reads an attribute; who writes it?

choices.text: Only the group's owners
choices.why: Owners cannot add members by hand to a dynamic group at all.

choices.text: Nobody: dynamic groups are fixed at creation
choices.why: They change all the time; that is their purpose.

choices.text: Any Global Administrator, by adding the user directly
choices.why: Direct additions are refused in a dynamic group; the rule is the membership.

choices.text: Anybody able to edit a user's department
choices.why: Right. Which is why the attribute should be one only the HR system writes.

prompt: A new tenant on the free tier tries to create the dynamic group of the lesson. What stands in the way?
hint: Dynamic groups have two limits.

choices.text: The rule needs a custom domain
choices.why: The rule reads attributes; domains have nothing to do with it.

choices.text: A subscription must exist first
choices.why: Groups live in the directory, which needs no subscription.

choices.text: Dynamic groups exist only for devices
choices.why: There are dynamic groups for users and for devices.

choices.text: A licence: dynamic groups need Entra ID P1
choices.why: Right. The paid tier, for the users they apply to.

prompt: `grp-shop-engineering` sits inside `grp-shop-all`. An application is assigned to `grp-shop-all`, and a role in a subscription too. What do the engineers get?
hint: Nesting is honoured per feature.

choices.text: Both, because membership is always transitive
choices.why: It is not, everywhere; the application assignment reads direct members only.

choices.text: The role, and not the application
choices.why: Right. Azure roles follow the nesting; assigning an application to a group does not.

choices.text: Neither, because nested groups are ignored by Azure
choices.why: Azure's role-based access follows the nesting.

choices.text: The application, and not the role
choices.why: It is the other way round.

prompt: What does an administrative unit let a company do?
hint: Management groups divide resources; what divides the directory?

choices.text: Bill each department for its own users
choices.why: Billing is the subscription's business, not the directory's.

choices.text: Give a group of users an Azure role on a subscription
choices.why: That is a role assignment to a group, lesson 9.

choices.text: Limit a directory role to a slice of the directory
choices.why: Right. A store manager resets passwords in her unit and nowhere else.

choices.text: Hide users from the rest of the directory
choices.why: Members stay visible; what changes is who can manage them.

prompt: The store manager holds User Administrator scoped to `au-shop-stores`. She tries to reset `bia`'s password. What happens?
hint: Is bia in the unit?

choices.text: It is refused: bia is outside her scope
choices.why: Right. The role reaches the unit's members only.

choices.text: It works, since User Administrator covers the tenant
choices.why: Only when given at the tenant. Here it was given on the unit.

choices.text: It works after bia approves it
choices.why: No approval exists for this; the scope decides.

choices.text: It is refused because she needs an Azure role too
choices.why: Azure roles have nothing to do with passwords.

prompt: A Global Administrator opens a virtual machine's page and is refused. What is the explanation?
hint: Two role systems share a word and nothing else.

choices.text: The machine is in another tenant
choices.why: Nothing says so; the refusal has a simpler cause.

choices.text: Global Administrators are blocked from resources by policy
choices.why: No policy is needed: the role never reached resources.

choices.text: The role expired after the first sign-in
choices.why: Directory roles do not expire on their own.

choices.text: Directory roles give no access to Azure resources
choices.why: Right. Until an Azure role says so, the directory's most powerful role reads no machine.

prompt: Match each role to the system it belongs to.
hint: Two systems: the directory's and Azure's.

pairs.right: a directory role, with the emergency bridge

prompt: Why does the Terraform file for the shop's directory need the `azuread` provider rather than `azurerm`?
hint: Which API does each one write to?

choices.text: Users and groups live in Microsoft Graph, not Resource Manager
choices.why: Right. `azuread` writes to Graph; `azurerm` to Resource Manager.

choices.text: Because Terraform allows one provider per directory
choices.why: A configuration can use several providers at once.

choices.text: Because `azurerm` is pinned to an older version
choices.why: Versions do not matter here; the API does.

choices.text: Because `azurerm` cannot run without a subscription
choices.why: Neither provider ran against Azure here; the question is which API owns the object.

prompt: The rule in `main.tf` is mistyped as `user.departmnt -eq "Engineering"`. Where is the mistake caught?
hint: What is the rule, to Terraform?

choices.text: By `terraform validate`, against Graph's schema
choices.why: To Terraform the rule is a string; the schema says nothing of its contents.

choices.text: By Entra ID, when the group is created
choices.why: Right. The lab checks the shape; the value is Entra ID's to judge.

choices.text: Never: the group is created empty and stays so
choices.why: Entra ID checks the rule when the group is created.

choices.text: By `terraform init`, when the provider is installed
choices.why: `init` reads no resource at all.

prompt: Put the shop's store-staff arrangement in the order it has to be built.
hint: A role cannot be scoped to a unit that does not exist.
items: add the store staff to the unit
give the store managers User Administrator scoped to the unit
check that a manager cannot reset `bia`'s password
trap: The check comes last: it is the test that the scope is the unit and not the tenant.

prompt: Which of these are principals, in Entra ID's sense? Choose all that apply.
hint: Something that can sign in, or be given a role.

choices.text: A user
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: A security group
choices.why: Right: it can be given a role.

choices.text: An administrative unit
choices.why: A unit is a scope roles are limited to, not a holder of roles.

choices.text: A managed identity
choices.why: Right, lesson 8.

choices.text: A resource group
choices.why: That is a scope of Azure roles, not something that receives them.

prompt: A colleague wants to use `shop.onmicrosoft.com` as the made-up tenant in a training script and query its discovery document. What does the lesson say about that name?
hint: Who owns an `.onmicrosoft.com` name?

choices.text: It is reserved for documentation, like `.example`
choices.why: Only `.example` is reserved. `.onmicrosoft.com` names belong to tenants.

choices.text: Entra ID refuses it with AADSTS90002
choices.why: That code came back for the made-up GUID, not for this name.

choices.text: It is a real tenant: somebody took the name first
choices.why: Right. Entra ID answers for it, so a script would be asking about a stranger's tenant.

choices.text: It works only after a DNS record is added
choices.why: That is how a custom domain is verified, not how this name works.

prompt: A user's ___ id never changes, while the name she types to sign in can.
hint: Every permission points at it.
